root_idea.summary: The root centers on making a mark or exerting an effect, with a related branch denoting strenuous striving, toil, and effortful earning.
root_idea.development: The physical sense of scratching or lacerating is presented as the underlying line from which exerted work and earning are developed. The Quranic forms use the labor-and-exertion branch for one who labors toward the Lord and for that labor itself.

senses.definition: One who labors and strives, exerting himself in work; in the Quranic usage, one laboring toward his Lord until the meeting with Him.
senses.usage_conditions: In كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ, the construction expresses sustained effort toward one's Lord, including work whose outcome is good or evil for the worker.

senses.definition: Strenuous striving, toil, and the hardship attending such effort.
senses.usage_conditions: In كَادِحٌ إِلَى رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا, the verbal noun denotes the exertion of laboring toward one's Lord.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or obtain sustenance for one's family; to gain, acquire, or earn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction كَدَحَ لِعِيَالِهِ, with the effort directed toward providing for a family or household.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scratch or lacerate a face, thereby disfiguring it; figuratively, to mar an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the face in the physical sense and with an affair in the figurative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scratch or lacerate intensely, repeatedly, or in many places.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensified Form II construction describing extensive or repeated scratching or laceration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate the hair with a comb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of combing or parting the hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A scratch or laceration of the skin; a mark made by scratching or biting, more extensive than خَدْش.
A lesser tooth-biting or tooth-abrading action, analogous to كَدْم.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported tooth-related use in which كَدْح denotes a degree below كَدْم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become scratched or lacerated repeatedly or extensively; to become badly broken in the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V construction describing a subject undergoing extensive bodily laceration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Much lacerated by the bites of other asses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of an ass, including a wild ass, whose skin has been lacerated by such bites.
